newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to allow Formosa to import naphtha in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to allow Formosa to import naphtha in 1998.

text.p: Taiwan's Energy Commission said on Monday it expected to bend regulations in early 1998 to allow Formosa Plastics to import naphtha -- the first step in ending Chinese Petroleum's oil-import monopoly.
"The commission should allow Formosa to import supplies for its new petrochemical complex to protect its (Formosa's) vested rights," a commission official told Reuters.
"The most likely way is to re-interpret the current regulation to allow Formosa's imports," added the official, who asked not to be identified.
The liberalisation would allow Formosa to import naphtha to supply its new US$9 billion petrochemical complex, where a naphtha cracker is expected to be completed in March 1998.
Formosa officials were not available for comment.

Taiwan's Energy Commission removed barriers to private oil imports in June 1996 but the market in effect remains closed because a qualifying clause limits import volume to less than 50 percent of an importer's annual oil production -- meaning firms with no production are ineligible to import.
On that basis, Chinese Petroleum will remain Taiwan's only oil producer and importer until Formosa opens the huge new refinery complex.
Formosa's naphtha cracker will have capacity to produce 450,000 tonnes of ethylene and 230,000 tonnes of cracked gasoline a year.
